newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia sees $550 mln quota in De Beers agreement.
newsitem.headline: Russia sees $550 mln quota in De Beers agreement.

text.p: Russia's main diamond producer Almazy-Rossii-Sakha (ARS) will have an annual export quota of at least $550 million under an agreement shortly to be signed with South Africa's De Beers, ARS spokesman Yuri Beskakotov said on Thursday.
Russia will have the right to sell five percent of the quota itself to monitor market conditions, he told Reuters.
Under the long-delayed agreement Russia will also be allowed to directly export additional diamonds outside the quota to the value of 25 percent of the quota, he said.

De Beers, which controls the world's diamond trade, sharply curtailed its purchases of Russian diamonds at the end of last year when Moscow failed to communicate its position on a draft agreement submitted to the cabinet in October 1996.

Russia's First Deputy Prime Minister Anatoly Chubais said this week the agreement would be signed no later than June 4. Previously, ARS, which last year produced about $1.35 billion of rough diamonds, sold 95 percent of its rough diamonds to De Beers and had the right to sell the remaining five percent in Moscow.
Russian diamonds accounted for 26 percent of De Beers' total worldwide sales under the previous contract, a deal worth about $1.2 billion a year to Russia.
